title: Efficient Topology-aware Data Augmentation for High-Degree Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Message-passing GNNs face severe over-smoothing and efficiency issues on high-degree graphs, and feature aggregation alone struggles to capture their rich structural semantics.

gap.claim: Existing GNN feature aggregation does not adequately address high-degree graph efficiency, over-smoothing, and complex structure semantics.

contributions.claim: TADA is an efficient front-mounted data augmentation framework for GNNs on high-degree graphs.
TADA combines feature expansion with structure embeddings and topology- and attribute-aware graph sparsification.
The framework uses efficient structure sketching to augment node features and removes redundant or noisy edges using task-relevant structural and attribute features.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report improved predictive performance for mainstream GNN models on eight real homophilic and heterophilic high-degree graphs for node classification.
The authors report efficient training and inference processes.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are widely used for learning on graph-structured data and commonly rely on recursive neighbor aggregation.
Neighbor aggregation creates over-smoothing and efficiency problems on high-degree graphs, while complex structural semantics are difficult to capture.
TADA addresses these limitations through structure-embedding feature expansion and topology- and attribute-aware graph sparsification.
The authors report better node-classification performance and efficient training and inference across eight real high-degree graphs.

source_observation.claim: High-degree graph message passing can suffer from over-smoothing, computational inefficiency, and inadequate structural representation.

interpretation.claim: Graph learning systems may benefit from explicitly representing structure and reducing edges that add little task-relevant information.

application.claim: For high-degree graphs, consider augmenting node features with structure embeddings and sparsifying topology using structural and attribute signals.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these techniques generalize beyond the reported high-degree graph settings or tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the eight datasets, baselines, or quantitative performance gains.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, computational measurements, or ablation results.
The abstract does not report limitations or conditions under which TADA may underperform.
